content:
In macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has put more effort into bug fixes and performance improvements. And so far in the beta, the quality-of-life improvement I've been most happy about is a Messages fix when logging into your Mac.

When you log into your macOS Golden Gate Mac, Messages should already be updated and synced.

One of the Mac's biggest advantages over PCs is how well it works with your iPhone.

Universal Clipboard, iPhone Mirroring, and Handoff let you seamlessly move between your iPhone and Mac.

But there's one place where macOS has long failed to provide a truly seamless experience: right after you first log in, Messages briefly falls out of sync.

We've all experienced this. Right after you log into your Mac, Messages notifications immediately start popping up in the top right corner — but for messages you've already read.

However, in macOS Golden Gate, as part of its focus on performance and polish, Apple has significantly improved how Messages syncs across your devices.

Apple says the syncing process is now more efficient. When your Mac comes online, the unread message count is more accurate right away, and you won't get notifications for messages you've already read.

I use my iPad Pro as my primary computer, with my Mac playing a supporting role. Messages sync between my iPhone and iPad has almost never given me trouble, so I've always been a bit annoyed that the experience was worse on Mac.

Now on macOS Golden Gate, that annoyance should be a thing of the past. At least based on the beta so far, Apple seems to have actually pulled it off.

How has Messages syncing been working for you in the macOS Golden Gate beta? Share your experience in the comments.
